front_blocks.md: Describe the **general structure** of an amino acid.

back_blocks.md: A central carbon bonded to:
**an amino group (–NH~2~)**, **a carboxyl group (–COOH)**, **a hydrogen atom** and **an R group** (variable side chain).

front_blocks.md: How is a **peptide bond formed**?

back_blocks.md: By a **condensation reaction** between the **amino group** of one amino acid and the **carboxyl group** of another.
A molecule of **water** is released.

front_blocks.md: How is a **peptide bond broken**?

back_blocks.md: By **hydrolysis** — a molecule of **water** is added, splitting the peptide bond.

front_blocks.md: Describe the **quaternary structure** of haemoglobin.

back_blocks.md: **Four polypeptide chains** — two **α (alpha)-globin** and two **β (beta)-globin** chains.

front_blocks.md: Why is haemoglobin an example of a **globular protein**?

back_blocks.md: It has a compact, rounded **3D shape** and is **soluble**, with a physiological role (**oxygen transport**).

front_blocks.md: How is the structure of haemoglobin **related to its function**?

back_blocks.md: Each of its **four haem groups** contains an iron ion (**Fe^2+^**) that binds **one O~2~** molecule.
So one haemoglobin molecule can carry **four oxygen molecules**.

front_blocks.md: Why is **iron** important in haemoglobin?

back_blocks.md: The **Fe^2+^ ion** in each **haem group** is where **oxygen binds**, allowing haemoglobin to transport oxygen.

front_blocks.md: Describe the structure of a **collagen** molecule.

back_blocks.md: **Three polypeptide chains** wound together in a **triple helix**.
The chains are held together by **hydrogen bonds**.

cards.front_md: Describe the structure of a **collagen** molecule.
cards.back_md:

The chains are held together by **hydrogen bonds**.

front_blocks.md: How are collagen molecules arranged into **fibres**?

back_blocks.md: Many collagen molecules line up in parallel, with **covalent cross-links** between them.
Their **staggered ends** add strength, forming strong collagen **fibres**.

cards.front_md: How are collagen molecules arranged into **fibres**?
cards.back_md:
Many collagen molecules line up in parallel, with **covalent cross-links** between them.

Their **staggered ends** add strength, forming strong collagen **fibres**.

front_blocks.md: How is the structure of collagen **related to its function**?

back_blocks.md: The **triple helix** and **cross-links** give very high **tensile strength**.
This makes it a strong structural protein in tendons, skin and artery walls.
